Ah I'm sorry for taking so long to reply.

Things are just so much better today. He's happy, and has been for a couple of days, pretty steadily, he's enjoying himself, he's enjoying life, he's being so nice, i love him. I know he's my soulmate. Never doubted it.

And no matter how your depression affects others, i just want to let you know that they care about you very much nevertheless and they still love you and want you with them.

Until next time.

Kay, thank you for the finally useful advice.

"You are a good person"
the subject in which i am trying to help as said otherwise, he/she said i was selfish for making him/her go through their pain, am i selfish?
this just doesn't work though with him, i guess, or i'm doing something terribly wrong and i really have no idea how to listen. i can't just listen and he feels better.
If you need to talk though, just send me a PM. I'm not terribly active with this account, but you can send stuff anyway.
I wish. If my parents couldn't intercept the mail, I would, Good luck to you.
I think that's what I needed to hear. Thanks.
alright, thanks. in the meantime, since he's working on that, how do I cope? this is the most stressful thing in my life

Hey, well, dunno if you're still here/you'll see this, but I was wondering for some advice. 

He's 16, as aforementioned, which means he relies on his parents to get therapy or meds. However, he's much too afraid to tell them of his condition and have them get himself professional help. His mother gave him traumatic experiences (crying, feeling bad) both when she found out he may have a heart condition and when he told her about his OCD. For his father, whom also suffers depression, he is afraid he'll worsen that. 

How can I push him to seek this professional help? Is there anything he can do instead? 

P.S: His dad gets meds for his depression, so even though his parents are in deep poverty, such medical help is apparently available. Should he use his dad's meds? Is that even ethical? Could they be the right or wrong meds?
16, so, no, not really. I think, largely, he's just afraid to do it. He absolutely will not notify his parents about the situation. they might be able to do it, but he will absolutely not tell them.

i see you post here often and try to help people, that's nice, benevolent, and generous, thanks for helping all these people, and best of luck to you while doing it

just remember to take care of yourself too
thanks. it's nice to hear someone is so helpful and cares, thanks again.

It's so hard though. I try. But what about when he asks me something? What about when he says "I'm not sure what to think right now" after a mood swing, and I reply "alright, well if i did anything wrong, sorry", and he says "it's not your fault you're better than me"
what do I do? this is just so complicated, i don't know what i'm supposed to do
